# git-snitch

> git-snitch is a Node-based npm CLI that writes self-contained HTML reports for a single git repository or a recursive directory scan. No backend, no database, no browser launch unless you ask for --open.

## TL;DR

- **What it is:** An npm CLI tool (`@git-snitch/cli`) that generates standalone HTML activity reports from git repositories.
- **Who it is for:** Engineering leads, auditors, and teams who need portable git evidence without setting up a hosted dashboard.
- **Key capabilities:** repo reports, scan reports, custom TSX templates, CSV/JSON export, privacy-first anonymization (--anon), GitHub metadata enrichment.
- **Technology:** TypeScript, Node.js, published on npm.
- **Install:** `npm install --save-dev @git-snitch/cli` or `pnpm add -D @git-snitch/cli`

## Canonical pages

- [Home](https://git-snitch.dbuild.dev/) - Marketing landing page with features, usage guide, and demo links.
- [Repo report demo](https://git-snitch.dbuild.dev/example.html) - Self-contained HTML report for a single repository.
- [Scan report demo](https://git-snitch.dbuild.dev/weekload.html) - Self-contained HTML report for a recursive directory scan.

## Key topics

- Git activity reporting: generating navigable HTML reports from git history.
- Repository health: contributor analysis, commit frequency, quality signals, hotspot detection.
- Scan comparison: recursively scanning multiple repositories and comparing them in one report.
- Privacy: anonymizing repo names, author emails, and file paths with --anon.
- Custom templates: route-level TSX overrides for report rendering.
- Standalone output: self-contained HTML files with no server dependency.
